source_text: Approbavit ergo Apostolus, quia non sit tantummodo scriptum propter Abraham, quod reputatum est illi ad iustitiam [n236] , sed et propter nos, quibus sine dubio reputatur, cum in Deum credimus, qui Iesum Christum ex mortuis excitavit, qui traditus est - inquit - propter delicta nostra et resurrexit propter iustificationem nostram [n237] .
pass_a_gloss: The Apostle therefore approved that it was not written only on account of Abraham, that it was reckoned to him unto justice, but also on account of us, to whom without doubt it is reckoned, when we believe in God, who raised Jesus Christ from the dead, who was handed over, he says, on account of our offenses and rose on account of our justification.

lemmas.lexica: LS delictum; Blaise Rom 5 delictum vs donum
LS iustificatio; Blaise forensic making-just, not later system

pass_b_english: The apostle therefore established that it was not written only for Abraham’s sake that faith was reckoned to him as righteousness (Romans 4:23), but also for ours. It is undoubtedly reckoned to us when we believe in God, who raised Jesus Christ from the dead: ‘Who was handed over,’ he says, ‘because of our offenses and rose because of our justification’ (Romans 4:24–25).

choices.why: Paul's delictum of the one man; an act, not a nature.
Paul's iustificatio vitae; keep forensic making-just, not a later systematic slogan as default.
